articles.headline: College basketball roundup: Stanford women match worst start since 2017, fall to Portland
keyFacts: The Stanford women's basketball team lost 73-62 to Portland on Sunday night, dropping to a 4-3 record and matching their worst start since 2017.
Portland scored 33 points off turnovers and was led by Sara Mangan, who scored 18 points off the bench.
Stanford guard Hailee Swain was held to 10 points on 4-for-14 shooting, while Inés Sotelo Míguez scored a team-high 18 points for the Cardinal.
body: Stanford women's basketball head coach Kate Paye reacts during the first half of the Cardinal's loss against the Washington Huskies on Friday at Alaska Airlines Arena in Seattle. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images)
The Stanford women's basketball team is off to its worst start since 2017 after falling to host Portland 73-62 on Sunday night.
The Cardinal (4-3) were outscored by eight in the fourth quarter and the Pilots (4-2) totaled 33 points off turnovers.
Point guard Hailee Swain, who entered averaging 20.5 points per game, was held to 10 on 4-for-14 shooting (0-for-5 from 3-point). Inés Sotelo Míguez scored a team-high 18
Sara Mangan led Portland with 18 points off the bench.
The last time these teams met, Stanford squandered a 13-point second-half lead to end its 2024-25 season in a 69-68 overtime defeat in the first round of the WBIT.

The 2017-18 Cardinal suffered losses to No. 5 Ohio State, No. 1 Connecticut and again against the Buckeyes (then ranked ninth) in their first seven games, only to finish second in the Pac-12 and advance to the Sweet Sixteen.
These 2026-27 Cardinal suffered losses to unranked Arizona and Portland sandwiched around a program-worst 55-point defeat to No. 16 Washington.

USF 81, Cal State-Bakersfield 58: The Dons built a 20-point halftime lead and breezed to the victory at home. Candy Edokpaigbe led USF (5-1) with 18 points and Aina Cargol and Lucia Yenes added 15 apiece. The Dons shot 50.9% from the field and 11-for-24 from 3-point range. Dresha Moore led Bakersfield (1-3) with 18 points.
Men

St. Mary's 94, Menlo 78: The Gaels had to overcome a surprisingly strong first half from the Division II Oaks from Atherton, leading just 43-41 at the half. But behind an overpowering effort on the boards (outrebounding Menlo 39-23) and led by a 20-point night from Lithuanian sophomore guard Mantas Juzenar, St. Mary's pulled away in the second half to improve to 6-1 on the season.

articles.headline: Trump says he wants "permanent" deal with Iran
keyFacts: President Trump said he wants a permanent deal with Iran to prevent the country from gaining nuclear weapons.
Bahrain reported an Iranian attack on an industrial facility, prompting the U.S. to warn citizens there of increased threats.
Iranian officials held talks with Qatari mediators, declaring that progress requires lifting the U.S. Strait of Hormuz blockade.
body: What to know about the Iran war:

- President Trump told Fox News on Saturday that he wants a "permanent" deal with Iran. On Thursday, he told an Israeli TV network that he's "not rushing" and could wait until 2027 to make a decision on his next move in the .

- But sources familiar with the matter told CBS News last week that Israel and the U.S. are considering in the short term, amid the Netanyahu administration's concerns about how rapidly Iran is rebuilding its weapons production capacity.

- Iran on Thursday rejected Mr. that it may be seeking to develop chemical or biological weapons. The foreign ministry said U.S. allegations "keep changing" and are following "the same fraudulent script" as the justification for the 2003 U.S. invasion of Iraq.
Houthi media say 4 dead in Saudi attack on key port city
Houthi media said Monday that a Saudi attack killed four people and wounded 18 in Yemen's key port city of Hodeida.
The Iran-backed fighters, who control large swathes of Yemen including Hodeida, are battling a Saudi-led coalition that backs Yemen's internationally recognized government.
The strike targeted a building belonging to Yemen's Public Telecommunications Corporation, the Houthis' Almasirah television channel wrote on X.
Riyadh didn't immediately comment on the report.
It came a day after the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched toward the kingdom's western Red Sea coast.
That region is home to major oil installations that Houthi fighters have attacked in recent weeks, along with strikes on airports and military sites.
Yemen, which has been embroiled in more than a decade of civil war, was sucked into the U.S.-Iran conflict in July when a truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government unraveled.
Since then, hostilities have left more than 1,600 people dead and more than 300,000 displaced in the country, the poorest on the Arabian Peninsula, according to the latest U.N. data.
Houthis say Saudi strike on Yemen capital wounds 6
Houthi rebels in Yemen reported an airstrike early Sunday in the capital, Sanaa.
A spokesperson for the Houthi-run Health Ministry, Anees al-Asbahi, said the strike hit a fuel station operated by the state-run oil company and wounded six workers.
The strike also damaged the company's building, al-Asbahi said.
The Red Sea port city of Mokha also came under fire on Sunday, Houthi-run television reported, as did the Haifan district in the southwestern province of Taiza.
The Houthis blamed Saudi Arabia for the airstrikes but didn't report any casualties from them.
Trump says Iran launched more drones and missiles in past week "than at any time for over a year"
President Trump on Sunday said Iran "has launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time for over a year," but they've caused no damage.
In a post on Truth Social, the president linked the midterm elections — in which in both chambers of Congress — to the escalation in the war with Iran.

"As everyone remembers, I predicted two things concerning the November 3rd Midterm Elections. One, that if the Democrats win, the Stock Markets would go down, substantially, which they have, and two, that the Islamic Republic of Iran, which has killed 81,000 protestors as of today, will grow more aggressive in their attacks, which has also occurred," Mr. Trump said.
Higher fuel prices triggered by the war caused economic concerns for Americans, and top Republicans, have partly attributed GOP election defeats to the war with Iran.
Mr. Trump on Sunday said voters "didn't understand" what their votes meant and called the election "very 'strange.'"

"Iranian leaders consider the Democrats weak, ineffective, and Country destroying, but I won't let that happen! Both the Dems and Iran fought like hell to keep the Oil price up as long as possible and, since the Election, the Oil price has dropped by a record level," he said. "Too bad the Voters didn't understand this before they pulled the trigger, but the whole Election was very 'strange.'"
Americans in Bahrain urged to practice "heightened vigilance" amid attacks threat increase

The U.S. Department of State Consular Affairs is urging Americans in Bahrain to practice "heightened vigilance" amid an increase in the threat of attacks by Iran and its allies on U.S. facilities in the region.

"Be aware of potential alerts, flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions," the department said in a security alert shared on social media. "Iran has launched attacks targeting U.S. assets in both Kuwait and Bahrain, and Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions."
UAE condemns "in the strongest terms" renewed attack in Bahrain
The United Arab Emirates on Sunday condemned "in the strongest terms" the renewed attack by Iran on Bahrain.
On Saturday, Bahrain's interior ministry said Iran had attacked a civilian industrial facility, sparking a fire and causing material damage. No injuries were reported.
It marked the fourth attempted attack by Iran in Bahrain in roughly a week, a sharp escalation following a relative lull of attacks linked to Iran on U.S.-associated targets in the Gulf.
The UAE's foreign ministry said that Saturday's attack "constitutes a flagrant violation" of Bahrain's sovereignty and a "threat to its security and stability."
"The Ministry reiterated the UAE's full solidarity with the Kingdom of Bahrain and its support for all measures aimed at safeguarding its security and stability," the ministry said in a post on X.
Athlete swims Strait of Hormuz to raise awareness of Iran war's toll on wildlife

British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh has swum in the North Pole and Antarctica to draw attention to environmental causes. But battling freezing waters and extreme conditions hasn't prepared him for his latest challenge: swimming the while tankers are attacked and blown up nearby.
Pugh, who is a United Nations Patron of the Oceans, spent three days this week swimming parts of the dangerous waterway to highlight how the threatens the area's habitat and wildlife.

Wearing only swimming trunks, goggles and a cap bearing the U.N. logo, the athlete started from the Musandam Peninsula, on the southern tip of the strait, and ended by rounding the Cape of Hormuz, completing about 9.3 miles in total. Pugh is believed to be the first person to undertake a long-distance swim there since the war started.
The swimmer said that minutes after he entered the water on Monday, he heard two loud explosions that rocked the sea.
Read more .
Bahrain says Iranian attack hit industrial facility
Bahrain's interior ministry said on Saturday that Iran had attacked a civilian industrial facility, sparking a fire and causing material damage, though no injuries were reported.

"As a result of the heinous Iranian aggression, a civilian industrial facility was targeted, causing a fire at the site. Civil Defence is working to bring the fire under control," the interior ministry said on X.
"Preliminary reports indicate material damage, with no injuries reported," it added, without specifying the site's location.
Bahrain is host of the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet.
A U.S. official told CBS News that Iran launched new attack attempts, but there were no impacts to U.S. forces or military assets in the region.

This latest incident marks the fourth attempted attack by Iran in Bahrain in roughly a week, a sharp escalation following a relative lull of about two months in attacks linked to Iran on U.S.-associated targets in the Gulf.
CBS/AFP
Iran holds talks with Qatari mediators
Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Saturday that a Qatari delegation visited Tehran the previous evening and "held two hours of talks," without providing details.
Negotiations between the U.S. and Iran to end the war have stalled in recent months.
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said, however, that ongoing talks in the region must be "given a chance" and that the ongoing U.S. blockade of the Strait of Hormuz "must be lifted rationally."
"Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless," he said, quoted by state television.
"At the same time, we have always affirmed our readiness for dialogue, just as we are ready to defend ourselves."
Iran's conditions have included ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the U.S. counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
-CBS/AFP
Gold Star families frustrated with Pentagon investigation into Iran drone strike that killed 6 soldiers

Gold Star families have told CBS News that briefings about a forthcoming U.S. military report on the in the Iran conflict did not, to their satisfaction, address their concerns about the military preparations and response to the attack.

Several of the families said they have been briefed about the unclassified results from the long-awaited internal probe into one of the first attacks on U.S. troops during Operation Epic Fury. were killed by a drone strike on in Kuwait, known as Port Shuaiba, on March 1.
The official report has not yet been released to the public. The Pentagon has indicated it could be made public in a matter of days.
Trump says he wants to make "permanent" deal with Iranian regime
President Trump said Saturday that he wants to make a "permanent" deal with Iran that will prevent the country from gaining a nuclear weapon in the future.

"What I'm doing is I'm going to make it so that if we have an incompetent president in four years or 15 years or 20 years, I'm going to make a deal that is going to be permanent," Mr. Trump told Fox News in a phone interview on Saturday. "I'm not going to let somebody allow them to have a nuclear weapon."

Mr. Trump said he's never "cared too much about the regime" leading Iran, and that he has "taken out two regimes already," though he declined to specify further. Former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed in the initial strikes on Iran that began the war in February 2026. His son Mojtaba Khamenei has held the title ever since.
Mr. Trump said Iranian officials have been "very, very difficult" to make a deal with.
"I mean, we make a deal and then they break the deal the next day," Mr. Trump said.
Iran state TV unveils new dual-missile launcher

Iranian state television aired footage from an underground missile facility where the paramilitary Revolutionary Guard unveiled a new launcher it said was capable of firing two liquid-fueled missiles.

The launchers appear to be an advance over a dual launcher that Iran previously used that fired two solid-fuel missiles at a time. Liquid fuel is more efficient and gives operators some capability to adjust the missiles' speed and trajectory.

The location of the missile site was not revealed, but the broadcast aimed to tout Iran's missile capabilities and counter past U.S. claims to have destroyed the missile program, amid fears that the war with the United States could heat up once again.

During the unveiling of the launchers, Brig. Gen. Seyyed Majid Mousavi, commander of the Guard's Aerospace Force, boasted that Iran's "capabilities have expanded significantly," adding, "We have integrated 'surprises' and highly effective assets into our combat structure."
2 tankers attacked in Strait of Hormuz, U.K. maritime agency says
Two tankers were attacked on Saturday in the Strait of Hormuz, at the heart of the conflict between Iran and the United States, British maritime agency UKMTO said.

"A tanker transiting outbound in the Strait of Hormuz has been hit on the stern by an unknown projectile. There are no reported casualties at this time," the agency said, adding that another tanker was struck in its engine room.
Also on Saturday, Iran said it shot down a U.S. drone over Qeshm Island in the strait, according to Iranian state TV.
American fighter jets struck an Iranian missile site on Qeshm last Tuesday, according to a U.S. military official.
Before the Middle East war, triggered by U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran in February, one fifth of the world's oil and natural gas passed through the Strait of Hormuz.
Tehran has since locked down the strait and regularly targets ships that attempt to pass without its authorisation.
Washington, in response, has imposed a blockade on Iranian ports, and its navy has been escorting tankers through the waterway.
Saudi-led coalition says it downed 3 Houthi missiles headed for Riyadh

Saudi-led coalition said it downed three Houthi missiles headed for Riyadh after two explosions were heard in the area early on Saturday morning local time, an AFP journalist in the Saudi capital reported.
"Air defences intercepted and destroyed (3) ballistic missiles launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Riyadh," the coalition said on X.
The blasts came after authorities issued an alert saying the city was "under a hostile aerial threat."
The Saudi civil defense later lifted the alert and declared that "the danger has passed."
Yemen's Houthis said on X that they were striking targets across Saudi Arabia, including in Riyadh.
The incident came after the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis attacked the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets in a "special operation" on Friday.
The Houthis had threatened reprisals.
Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighboring Yemen's civil war, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognized government against the Houthis.
Opposition leader vows to form new Israeli government to oust Netanyahu swiftly
Gadi Eisenkot, who has been tasked with forming the next Israeli government, vowed Friday not to let coalition-building talks drag on as his wide-ranging bloc faces divisions on the way forward.

The former military chief's remarks appear as a warning to his own camp, which is split over whether to forge alliances with ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties, Arab-majority lists, or to form a national unity government that would leave current Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the role as a caretaker.
Sources told CBS News this week that a new offensive against Iran in collaboration with the U.S.

"I have no intention of letting this drag on. When the time is right, I will bring a new government before the Knesset for its approval, a good government that I will lead," Eisenkot said in a social media post.

Eisenkot has until next month to form a government to replace Netanyahu, after the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either of them. While denying any attempt to force through a coalition, Eisenkot stressed the need to act fast.

"We are in very dangerous territory. The outgoing prime minister is acting in ways we have never seen before," he said. "Military priorities have become entangled with political interests, and the timetable for military operations with the political calendar."
The AFP contributed reporting.
Tanker in the Strait of Hormuz struck by projectile, says naval monitor
A tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was struck by a projectile Friday, causing a fire onboard the vessel but no injuries, according to a British naval monitor.
The tanker was traveling out of the key waterway when it was struck by an unknown projectile, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations center.
The UKMTO earlier reported that a bulk carrier traveling east in the Gulf of Aden, off the southern coast of Yemen, had reported shots being fired in its vicinity by assailants on a small boat.
Trump says he, Putin and Xi talked about Iranian nuclear threat
During Friday's news conference, President Trump said that during his trilateral with Russia's President Vladimir Putin and China's Xi Jinping, the three leaders discussed nuclear responsibilities.

Mr. Trump said they "spoke about the need to cooperate to stop the proliferation of that nuclear threat throughout our planet" and that "in particular, we talked extensively about ensuring that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon."
Trump says U.S. wants "real deal" with Iran
As he lauded slightly lower gas prices at the White House on Friday, President Trump said the U.S. wants a "real deal" with Iran, not a "fake" deal.
"They want to make a deal but they don't want to make a deal that's acceptable to me," he said.
"They've been bulls******g people for 51 years," the president said of Iran.
CENTCOM denies U.S. strike as Iranian news agency reports missile hitting Qeshm Island

U.S. Central Command denied carrying out any new strikes on Iran's strategic Qeshm Island on Friday after Iran's Tasnim news agency, which is closely linked with the country's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, said a missile had hit the island in the Strait of Hormuz.

Tasnim said it had no information of any possible damage, and other Iranian media outlets offered more vague details. The semi-official Fars news agency said an explosion was heard in the skies over the island, but that the cause was unknown.
The U.S. has attacked the island several times, with what a military official described to CBS News as precision strikes on an IRGC missile site.
The official said that strike was launched "in self-defense … in response to IRGC aggression targeting U.S. personnel and assets."
Saudi Arabia intercepts 2 Houthi missiles, coalition says
The Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen said Friday that it had intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis.
Saudi Arabia backs Yemen's government in the impoverished nation's more than decade-long civil war against the Iran-backed rebel group.

The latest missiles launched by the Houthis targeted the Jazan region, on the southwest Saudi coast near the border with Yemen, but "air defense intercepted and destroyed" them, according to coalition spokesperson Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki.
The Houthis struck a tower in Riyadh's financial district earlier this week.
Cargo ship reports being fired on by assailants in small boat in Gulf of Aden
A bulk carrier traveling east in the Gulf of Aden, off the southern coast of Yemen, has reported shots being fired in its vicinity by armed men on a small boat, according to a British naval monitor.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations center, which is run by the British navy, said Friday that the ship was traveling eastbound when it was approached "by a dark blue skiff with six unidentified, armed persons on board."

"Four shots were fired in quick succession from the skiff and warning shots were returned by the armed security team onboard the bulk carrier," UKTMO said, adding that there was no damage reported to the vessel or its crew.
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis issue evacuation warning for Riyadh's financial district
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis urged people to avoid Riyadh's financial district Friday as the group issued a series of threats against Saudi Arabia.

"We announce that (King Abdullah Financial District) in the Saudi enemy's capital, Riyadh, is a military target for our forces. We therefore call on all employees, workers and citizens to stay away from it immediately," military spokesman Yahya Saree posted on X.

In a Telegram post Friday, Saree wrote: "We renew our warning to all investment companies, investors and capital to leave Saudi Arabia immediately and move to safe countries. Saudi Arabia is not safe except for the holy areas in Mecca and Medina."
Saudi Arabia of damaging a skyscraper in Riyadh's financial district with a strike earlier this week.
CBS/AFP
U.S. and Israel considering new assault on Iran, sources say
Israel and the U.S. are considering launching a new in the short term, according to sources familiar with the matter.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's administration is concerned about how rapidly the Iranians are rebuilding their ballistic missile manufacturing capabilities and the pace at which Iran is working to shield its military and nuclear infrastructure from attack by moving it underground, the sources told CBS News.

Months of indirect negotiations between the U.S. and Iran have failed to bring a ceasefire deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran has refused to even discuss its nuclear program unless the U.S. lifts its naval blockade and accepts six other key conditions.
Israel's military is prepared for a new round of fighting with Iran and is in peak defensive posture to respond to any first attack by Iran, the sources told CBS News.

The Netanyahu administration would prefer to launch a new joint operation with the U.S., but the sources told CBS News it remains unclear whether Mr. Trump wants to order new military action, and if so, what kind.

For both Mr. Trump and Netanyahu, who jointly launched the war with Iran almost nine months ago with a massive round of strikes on the Islamic Republic, the window for any new collaborative action may be closing.
Saudi's fight with Iran-backed Houthis intensifies as civilians warned to evacuate area around Yemeni port

The Saudi-led military coalition fighting in the escalating conflict with Iran's Houthi allies warned civilians Friday to leave the area around the key port of Hodeidah on Yemen's Red Sea coast, which has been held by the rebels for years.

The warning, issued in a social media post by the coalition's Saudi spokesman, suggested Saudi airstrikes on the port could be imminent. It came after Houthi authorities accused Saudi forces of killing 19 people earlier Friday with an attack that hit a civilian boat.

Yemen's civil war flared back up in July as the U.S. and Israeli war with Iran sent regional tension soaring. While the Yemen war started more than a decade ago with the Iran-backed Houthis seizing a huge portion of the country, including capital city Sanaa, it had been relatively calm for years until this summer.

Houthi health ministry spokesman Anees Alasbahi on Friday accused Saudi forces of a "horrific massacre" for the strike on the boat, which the rebels say killed civilians who had been displaced from their homes by the war.

Earlier Friday, the Saudi coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile and two drones fired at the kingdom's southern region, and the Saudi civil defense agency issued warnings of "potential danger" for the cities of Jizan and Abha, as well as the Khamis Mushait Governorate — all in the south.
They later said the danger had passed.
CBS/AFP
Trump's comments on chemical and biological weapons follow "same fraudulent script," Iranian official says

Iran's foreign ministry rejected on Thursday President Trump's accusation that the country may be seeking to develop chemical or biological weapons, comparing the claims to then-Secretary of State Colin Powell asserting to the United Nations that Iraq had obtained weapons of mass destruction.

"After the grand narrative of the 'Iranian nuclear threat,' U.S. officials are now claiming that there are indications Iran is developing biological or chemical weapons!" Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said in a post on X. "The allegations keep changing, but the underlying narrative remains disturbingly familiar. Once again, the world is apparently expected to suffer a bout of collective amnesia."

Baqaei cited the U.S. invasion of Iraq in 2003, which Washington justified with the claim of weapons of mass destruction being developed by Saddam Hussein's government, and asked why Americans would fall for it again.

"Do American officials really expect the world to forget Colin Powell's infamous appearance before the U.N. Security Council in 2003, when he held up a small vial as a visual representation of the alleged threat posed by Iraq's weapons of mass destruction?" he asked. "That moment has since become an enduring symbol of one of the most consequential intelligence failures and political deceptions in modern history."
"Now we find ourselves facing ominous new allegations and a narrative that appears to be following the same fraudulent script," he said.

Mr. Trump on Wednesday said there was an "indication" Iran was looking to develop chemical or biological weapons because the U.S. had "shut them out" of obtaining nuclear weapons, though he offered no evidence to support the claim.
Iran war powers measure again falls short in Senate

The Senate rejected a House-adopted resolution aimed at reining in President Trump's ability to strike Iran, losing Republican support despite frustration with the war following the party's losses in the midterm elections.

In a 48 to 51 vote, three Republicans — Sens. Susan Collins of Maine, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and Rand Paul of Kentucky — joined all but one Senate Democrat — Sen. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania — in support of the measure.

Thursday's vote marked the first time either chamber has weighed in on the war since the midterm elections, which dealt Republicans sweeping losses. Voters cited the war in Iran, and its toll on the economy, as among their top concerns.
The resolution would have directed the president "to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran," but its impact would have been largely symbolic.
Trump says he's "not rushing" to make decision on Iran, will wait until new year
President Trump told Channel 12 News in Israel that he is in no hurry to make any decisions on the war with Iran, and could in fact wait until next year.
"I'm not rushing to make any decisions on Iran," Mr. Trump told Keshet 12's Barak Ravid, who spoke to the president as he returned from China. "We'll see what happens after the new year starts."
The story noted Mr. Trump could also change his mind, though.

The tone seems in line with his and Secretary of State Marco Rubio's comments from last week. Mr. Trump called new strikes "quite unlikely," while Rubio said new strikes weren't needed since the economic sanctions campaign was working so well.
In an interview with Fox News on Wednesday, Mr. Trump said he had no need to ask China or Russia for help with an Iran deal.

"They want to make a deal, so I don't need help," Mr. Trump told the network. "I mean, I'm not going to go in asking for help. And frankly, they've treated us very well. They haven't fired. They haven't put ships in the water."

articles.headline: 'We failed the exam!' - Cristian Chivu fumes as 'soft and shallow' Inter throw away two-goal leads three times in chaotic Atalanta draw
keyFacts: Inter head coach Cristian Chivu criticized his team for mental fragility after they squandered a two-goal lead three times in a 4-4 draw against Atalanta.
Pio Esposito scored his first Serie A hat-trick for Inter during the match, which was ruined by Atalanta securing a dramatic point with a stoppage-time penalty.
Chivu stated that Inter must respond to the setback and improve their defensive intensity in upcoming fixtures.
body: FBL-ITA-SERIEA-ATALANTA-INTER MILAN - AFP Inter head coach Cristian Chivu has delivered a stinging assessment of his side's mental fragility after they squandered multiple leads in a breathtaking 4-4 draw against Atalanta. The Nerazzurri boss claimed his players "failed the exam" during a chaotic evening in Bergamo that saw them surrender a two-goal cushion on three separate occasions.
Late collapse ruins Pio Esposito's hat-trick

Atalanta snatched a dramatic point in Bergamo through Charles De Ketelaere’s second goal and a stoppage-time penalty from Franck, cancelling out Petar Sucic’s spot-kick that had made it 4-2. That late collapse ruined a landmark evening for Pio Esposito , who followed up his strong Nations League displays for Italy by netting his first Serie A hat-trick.

Inter’s frustration was compounded by two penalty calls. The visitors felt Davide Zappacosta deserved a red card rather than a booking for a goal-line elbow clearance, before Alessandro Bastoni conceded the decisive late spot-kick for an unintentional handball with his arms raised above his shoulder.
Chivu slams 'soft and shallow' Nerazzurri display

Speaking to DAZN Italia , Chivu lambasted his side's lack of edge. "We were leading 2-0, 3-1 and 4-2, so this is the regret," Chivu said after the game. "We had an idea of what we should’ve done and did not do, we should’ve controlled the advantage, then when we felt them snapping at our heels, we immediately restored the two-goal cushion.

"I think we failed the exam in the final minutes. It’s hard to say why we were unable to control the lead. We have to congratulate Atalanta, as they sensed that we were a bit shallow, and pumped crosses into the box, put bodies in there, while we were a little soft compared to our usual approach.
"I’m sorry, I see this as two gifted points, but we will learn from it and know now to let the intensity and mentality drop in the next games."

He also pinpointed lapses at set-pieces and inside the box. "The second Atalanta goal came from a corner, identical to one where Pepo had just made a great save moments earlier, so we did not learn from it," Chivu continued. "When we got to 4-2, our defence was then static in a chaotic situation. We need a certain determination and focus in these situations, and we were negligent in that area today."

Chivu altered his wide setup late on, though he insisted mentality mattered most. "I felt we were suffering on the wings, partly because we were too soft, we were allowing the space to put the crosses in too easily. I decided to put Marcus Thuram wide to help out Djed Spence in the final stages," Chivu added. "It’s a matter of desire to go into the duels, to be more determined, not just put bodies behind the ball, because if you don’t have the right intensity then a single error can be costly."
Defensive leaks undermine Inter's high ambitions

Although this marked Inter’s first draw of the season alongside 11 wins and three defeats in all competitions, their rearguard struggles stand out. They have leaked 17 goals in 12 Serie A matches - more than any other top-six club.

Asked whether that defensive record concerns him more than the dropped points, Chivu demanded a swift reaction. "We are conceding too many goals for a club that has high ambitions, but we must do like we did in Rotterdam and with Como, respond to a setback, not look over our shoulders to the past. We must learn that we cannot just control a situation, we’ve got to keep giving 100 per cent until the final whistle," the Inter coach concluded.
Focus turns to restoring intensity for upcoming fixtures

Inter must now turn the page quickly without dwelling on missed opportunities, using previous bounce-back displays in Rotterdam and against Como as their blueprint. With 11 victories from 15 games across all competitions, Chivu's side remain formidable when focused, provided they cut out individual errors and maintain full intensity until full-time.

articles.headline: MotoGP maestro Marquez makes history with eighth premier-class world title
keyFacts: Ducati rider Marc Marquez won his eighth premier-class MotoGP world title after finishing eighth at the Portuguese Grand Prix.
Marquez achieved his historic title following a remarkable comeback season that included overcoming injuries and double surgery.
Aprilia rider Marco Bezzecchi won the Portuguese Grand Prix race, with Jorge Martin finishing second ahead of the season finale in Valencia, Spain.
body: Spaniard Marc Marquez has been crowned MotoGP world champion for a record-equalling eighth time, screaming with joy at the Portuguese Grand Prix after a remarkable comeback this season.
Ducati rider Marquez finished eighth on Sunday as Italian Marco Bezzecchi rode to victory in southern Portugal, but it was enough to seal a second consecutive world title.
On crossing the line, the 33-year-old Marquez leapt from his bike and was hoisted up by his team before he ran towards his fans screaming with his arms aloft.
“We need to be happy. I know that we are here celebrating a historic moment. I know how I suffered,” said an emotional Marquez, who underwent double surgery midway through the season.
“I know that in the middle of the season, the fans believed more than I did. My people believed more than I did. But I kept pushing; I kept doing my best.
“I said last year that it was a championship where I was at peace with myself. This one is for all the fans that believed in me from 2020 until now. So thanks to all of you, this is for all of you.”
His eighth success in the premier class of motorcycling pulled Marquez level with Italian great Giacomo Agostini, who won his titles between 1966 and 1975.

As a final flourish, the Spaniard ascended a staircase accompanied by the silhouette of a goat on the screen, a nod to his growing ‘Greatest of All Time’ status, before receiving a golden commemorative helmet from Agostini himself.
He then attached another plaque with his name engraved on it on the Tower of Champions before embracing and lifting it over his head.

Marquez’s latest triumph is even more remarkable given the Spaniard’s injury- and crash-blighted campaign in which he had to wait until the eighth race in Hungary on June 7 before claiming his first win.

Marquez suffered a flat tyre in the season-opener in Thailand in March, fell at the Spanish GP in Jerez and again at the French GP where he picked up a foot fracture which ruled him out of the following race, the Catalan GP.
Making his comeback at the Italian GP in Mugello, he trailed Bezzecchi by 102 points in early June, just weeks after undergoing foot surgery on top of a previous operation on his injured shoulder.
But the Spaniard managed to bounce back once again, defying those who had already written him off.
Once he got rolling, he roared into a regular winning run with seven Grands Prix and 10 sprint race victories in all this season.

While not as obviously dominant as winning 11 GPs in the 2025 season, when an unexpected return to form following his 2024 switch to Ducati gave him a new lease of life, the latest win is as impressive.
Marquez had been the youngest-ever premier-class champion in his debut season in 2013 for Honda and then went on to win the title in five of the next six seasons.
He also overtook his great rival Valentino Rossi, who won seven MotoGP titles, although the swashbuckling Italian has 89 individual race wins in the top category compared with Marquez’s 80.
Having crashed during Saturday’s sprint race, Marquez rode out Sunday’s GP safely, needing only to finish in the top nine to secure his 10th title across all categories combined.
Aprilia’s Bezzecchi won Sunday’s race to complete the double in Portugal, having also won the sprint, with his stablemate Jorge Martin of Spain crossing in second.
With a total of 439 points and seven victories this year, this was enough for Marquez to keep his rivals at bay.
Martin is second with 396 points but only one win, and Bezzecchi, who has 394 points and seven first-place finishes, is third ahead of the season finale in Valencia, Spain, next weekend.
“Thank you for this bike,” Marquez told his team Ducati during his victory lap.

articles.headline: Germany news: Metalworkers go on strike as pay dispute heats up
keyFacts: The union IG Metall called for a strike affecting around 23,000 metalworkers across northern Germany in an ongoing pay dispute.
Union demands include a 5% wage increase, while employers have offered a 1.3% wage increase starting in July 2028.
Police suspect aggravated arson after a hospital fire in Berlin injured 15 people on Sunday evening.
body: What you need to know
- Germany's biggest union IG Metall is calling for metal workers to go on strike, affecting factories across much of northern Germany. It centers around a pay dispute that's been heating up for weeks
- German President Frank Walter Steinmeier heads to several African countries for a 4 day visit focusing on economic cooperation and the training of skilled workers
- A fire at a Berlin hospital has left at least 15 people injured with the police suspecting arson
- A key survey is expected to give insights about how Germans are thinking about foreign policy issues at a time of intense geopolitical tensions.
Read below for more on these stories and all other things Germanyon Monday, November 23.
Patient suspected of starting fire in Berlin hospital
Police are investigating a suspected case of aggravated arson after a fire broke out at a hospital in Berlin.
Investigators believe a patient set fire to his bed in a room on the first floor of one of the hospital buildings in the Lichtenberg district on Sunday evening.
One nurse and the suspected arsonist suffered smoke inhalation and had to be treated in hospital. Overall, 15 people were injured with another 13 suffering from minor injuries.
While firefighters managed to put out the flames, smoke spread to other parts of the hospital which then had to be evacuated.
Widespread strikes expected across Germany
The country's largest and most powerful union, the IG Metall, has called for a strike this Monday over an ongoing pay dispute.

The union has called on some 23,000 workers to down tools in as many as 19 factories in northern Germany. Among the companies affected likely to be impacted are Siemens, Mercedes Benz, and shipyard Meyer Werft.
At a similar strike on Friday, more than 12,000 workers had taken part.
IG Metall hopes that the strikes will increase pressure on employers to yield to its demands, which include a 5% wage increase.
Employers have so far offered a one-off payment next year and a 1.3% wage increase from July 2028.
Welcome to our coverage
Welcome and guten Morgen from the DW newsroom in Bonn!

Another busy week is kicking off and in large parts of Germany it starts with workers are walking off the job today in what is becoming a very heated dispute over pay. Factories from Mercedes Benz to the large shipmakers will likely be affected.
Berlin woke up this morning to news of a fire in the Lichtenberg part of the city, leaving at least 15 people injured. Police have described it as a serious case of arson.
And the country's president, Frank-Walter Steinmeier, is off for a trip to Africa which over the next few days that will take him to Ivory Coast, Ghana and Kenya.
We'll cover all those stories and whatever else hits the headlines across Germany so stay tuned.

articles.headline: Burnham to tell MPs 'landmark' EU deal could make next decade 'much better'
keyFacts: Prime Minister Andy Burnham will tell Parliament on Monday that a new EU deal could add seventeen billion pounds to the economy and improve the next decade.
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, and former prime ministers criticised the deal over Brussels rule alignment and political division.
Over the coming months, both sides will conduct an informal brainstorming process to explore options for the United Kingdom's long-term relationship with the EU.
body: - Published
The prime minister will tell Parliament on Monday the "landmark" deal struck with the EU means there is a "very real prospect" the next decade can be "much better" than the last one.
The deal is a "choice between a broken status quo or change", Andy Burnham will tell MPs.
He will also call it "the single biggest growth measure to be delivered in this parliament" - repeating his claim it could add Â£17bn to the British economy.

The PM described it on Friday as a "win-win" deal with the EU on British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme. But since then a host of politicians have criticised the plan, with one former prime minister urging him to "move on" from Brexit.
Burnham believes the agreement reached in Brussels "holds out the very real prospect that the next decade can be a much better one for Britain than the one we have just lived through".
"The ability to draw a line on a decade of drift and division is in our hands and I believe we should take it," he will say in his speech.
He will also paint the move as a choice "between easing pressure on the cost of living or allowing food prices to rise further" and "creating opportunities for young people or denying them".
He believes polling suggests the UK public "want closer ties" with the EU and the deal "delivers that".
But his announcement on Friday was greeted with a chorus of criticism from a number of opposing political figures.
Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said the deal was unfair because UK farmers would now have to follow rules made by Brussels.
She questioned the Treasury's analysis, which Burnham said suggested the deal "will add up to 0.5%" to UK gross domestic product and he described it as a "Â£17bn boost to the British economy".
Badenoch accused him of having "plucked that figure out of the air" before saying "the only modelling I've seen that even talks about that figure says it's actually 0.0%".

Meanwhile Reform UK leader Farage called the deal a "very good day for the EU", before adding: "A good day to try and humiliate the one member state that actually had the courage to say, 'We don't need to be part of you, we can govern our own country'."

Farage, who was a leading figure in the 2016 campaign to get Britain out of the EU, added in a social media post: "Like every prime minister before him, Burnham is a total fraud. Only Reform will stop the endless betrayal of the British people."
Over the weekend former prime ministers including Theresa May, Sir Tony Blair and Rishi Sunak also criticised the EU-UK deal.
May, who presided over three years of Brexit negotiations during her premiership, said she was "aghast" by the deal and warned Andy Burnham should "move on".
Sir Tony, who was a prominent opponent of leaving the EU, told The Sunday Times Britain should only rejoin the EU if it reforms, and allows more innovation on technology.
Former PM Sunak warned that reopening the debate about rejoining the EU could become a "huge distraction" for the current Labour government.
"Obviously it's divisive. But we saw last time around, it was also all consuming", he told Sky News in an interview airing in full on Tuesday.
Badenoch will use her speech at the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) annual conference on Monday to criticise Burnham's EU deal.
She will accuse the prime minister of securing a "terrible" deal and will say he should be "aiming a lot higher" in terms of driving growth.
Farage will tell the same conference that establishing closer ties with the EU would be a "disaster" for British businesses.
Rejoining the EU will hit the small firms that do not even trade with Europe with more red tape, more compliance costs, more Brussels rules they never asked for, he is expected to say.
On Friday, the PM said that over the coming months both sides will "seek to conduct an informal brainstorming process" to look at the options for the UK's "long-term relationship" with the EU.
He was also clear that the deal he struck was "probably the limit of what we can achieve in this Parliament, given what needs to be done to implement it".
He added: "But we want to inform the Parliament after this one, so that decisions can be taken about that long-term relationship."

articles.headline: Gukesh vows to win world chess title ‘all over again’ as Sindarov challenge looms
keyFacts: World chess champion Gukesh Dommaraju and challenger Javokhir Sindarov face each other in a historic 14-game title match in Geneva starting Tuesday.
Both 20-year-old grandmasters met the media on Sunday, with Gukesh stating he approaches the defense aiming to win the title again.
The winner of the 2.5 million dollar prize fund match will be the first player to reach seven and a half points.
body: World chess champion Gukesh Dommaraju insisted he was approaching his first title defense with the mindset of a challenger on Sunday as he and Javokhir Sindarov faced the media ahead of their historic showdown in Geneva, the youngest matchup in the 140-year history of the sport’s most coveted title.

The two 20-year-old grandmasters appeared side by side at the United Nations’ European headquarters in Geneva, where they struck a respectful tone before their best-of-14-games encounter begins on Tuesday at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, the affluent suburb overlooking Lake Geneva.
Pressed on whether defending a world championship was more difficult than winning it the first time, Gukesh politely rejected the premise.
“I don’t think I’m here to defend anything,” the Indian said. “I’m here to win it all over again. That’s the mindset I’m in.”

Sindarov, the fast-rising Uzbek challenger roughly six months older than Gukesh who enters the match as the oddsmakers’ favorite despite being a relative newcomer to the game’s highest level, was similarly reluctant to dole out predictions. Asked to assess his chances of becoming world champion, he put them at a diplomatic 50%.
“It’s a hard match and 14 games,” Sindarov said. “Everything can happen.”
The contest brings together two players whose careers have traced sharply divergent trajectories since Gukesh became the 18th and youngest ever undisputed champion in December 2024.

The Chennai native, who was only 18 when he defeated China’s Ding Liren to shatter the age record previously held by Garry Kasparov, has struggled badly for form since reaching the summit. After climbing to a career-high No 3 in the world that month, he has plummeted to No 26 following an extended string of underwhelming performances, making him the lowest-ranked reigning world champion since Elo ratings were introduced in 1971.

Sindarov, meanwhile, has surged from No 25 a year ago to a career-best No 4 after a breakthrough 12-month stretch that included winning the Fide World Cup in Goa last November and an unbeaten masterclass at this year’s Candidates Tournament in Cyprus, where he finished with six wins and eight draws against a stacked field including Fabiano Caruana, Hikaru Nakamura and Anish Giri to earn a shot at Gukesh’s title.

The 22-place gap between them is the widest of any world championship matchup since the title was reunified in 2006. Sindarov also holds a 2½-½ advantage in their three previous classical meetings, with two wins and one draw.
Yet both men played down the significance of past results on Sunday.
“Whatever has happened till now, I think just gets erased when we sit at the table for Game 1,” Gukesh said. “It’s a completely different match, completely different opponent and different place.”
He acknowledged Sindarov’s sustained run of success, describing the Tashkent-born challenger as one of the world’s strongest players and predicting a formidable assignment.
“Sindarov has just been in very consistent and very good form,” Gukesh said. “It’s for sure going to be a real test.”
Sindarov was equally complimentary about the champion, pointing to his extraordinary performances in winning the title as evidence that his recent difficulties should not be overinterpreted.

“Gukesh’s performance in 2024 is something fantastic,” Sindarov said, adding that he had experienced the Indian’s strength firsthand in January when they played to a 78-move draw at the prestigious Tata Steel tournament in Wijk aan Zee. “Sometimes you have some bad periods.”

The two players also revealed contrasting approaches to preparing for the championship. While Gukesh deliberately pared back his tournament schedule this year, Sindarov continued regularly entering competitions against elite opposition, reasoning that he needed more experience at the highest level.
Sindarov added that he had accepted an invitation to the four-month Grand Chess Tour circuit before winning the Candidates and saw little reason to withdraw afterward.
“Even after I won Candidates, I wanted to have more experience because I didn’t play that many strong tournaments in my career,” he said. “I’m happy with my decision.”

Gukesh said the strategy had not surprised him or his team, who expected the challenger to take advantage of his momentum and accumulate experience against the world’s strongest players. The trade-off was that Sindarov’s busy slate also gave Gukesh and his team a wealth of recent games to study for clues about the challenger’s approach.

The preparations have also given Sindarov an appreciation for the peculiar demands of a world title match. He once found it difficult to believe that players could spend three or four months preparing to face a single opponent. Now, having devoted much of the past six months to the task himself, he wonders whether even that is enough.
“I was thinking six months is enough time,” he said. “But maybe even this six months ... is also maybe not enough to prepare for such a hard tournament.”

The Indian, by contrast, can draw on his experience in the pressure-cooker environment of the world championship stage, where the psychological and physical demands of facing the same opponent for weeks on end can be as punishing as the chess itself. Gukesh said he had been surfing, running and spending time outdoors, while Sindarov has taken up padel, playing regularly during his training camp.
“If I would be, like, 30, 40, maybe it will be tough,” Sindarov said. “But because I’m young, I think it’ll be not very hard, like, physically.”

Gukesh will again work with Polish grandmaster Grzegorz Gajewski, who helped guide his successful 2024 campaign, as well as South African mental conditioning coach Paddy Upton, who was part of the backroom staff for India’s cricket team when they won the 2011 World Cup and the Indian men’s hockey team when they claimed bronze at the Paris Olympics in 2024. Sindarov revealed he is working with Ukrainian coach Roman Vidonyak, although neither player has publicly disclosed the full composition of his team of seconds, the trusted advisers responsible for preparing openings and analyzing the opponent.

The match will be staged at the Fondation Martin Bodmer, a museum and research library housing rare manuscripts and books, including a Gutenberg Bible, a Shakespeare First Folio and a first edition of Isaac Newton’s Principia. Both players inspected the playing hall on Saturday ahead of Monday’s technical meeting.

Unlike most recent world championship tilts, the players will not compete inside a purpose-built soundproof enclosure. Fide has abandoned the familiar transparent cube in order to preserve the atmosphere of the historic venue, relying instead on enhanced security measures and strict limits on the number of spectators and media admitted to the playing hall.

Sindarov admitted that he had expected to play inside the traditional fishbowl, but was impressed by the stage. “The playing hall is really very beautiful,” he said. Gukesh, meanwhile, said he had checked the chairs, lighting and even the floor to ensure he would be comfortable during games that could last four or five hours – and occasionally even longer. As for the rare books surrounding the board, the champion admitted he had barely looked at them. “I don’t think I’ll be reading in between the games,” he joked.

The glass enclosure, designed to shield players from distractions, was first used during Garry Kasparov’s 1995 title defense against Viswanathan Anand at New York’s World Trade Center and has featured in numerous subsequent championships, including Gukesh’s victory over Ding in Singapore two years ago. Sindarov admitted the setting would take some getting used to, having never played a tournament in which there was nobody else competing nearby.

The match carries a $2.5m (£1.9m) prize fund, with $200,000 awarded for each decisive game and the remainder divided equally between the players. Sindarov will open with the white pieces on Tuesday after the drawing of lots at Sunday’s opening ceremony, with the players alternating colors throughout the match. The first to reach seven and a half points will be crowned champion, with rapid and blitz tiebreaks scheduled if the contest finishes level after 14 games. Three of the past five world title matches have been deadlocked after the classical portion and required tiebreaks: 2016, 2018 and 2023.

The winner will join or continue a centuries-spanning lineage stretching back to Wilhelm Steinitz, who became the first official world champion in 1886. Gukesh is seeking to retain the crown he won as a teenager, while Sindarov is attempting to become the first player from Uzbekistan to capture the title.
For now, neither is allowing himself to dwell too much on what victory might mean.
Sindarov, who will turn 21 on 8 December, the scheduled date of Game 12, said he had made no pledges or wagers about how he might celebrate winning the championship.
“I really want to focus on my next 20 days and try to play my best chess,” he said. “Then we’ll see.”
Gukesh, who celebrated his 2024 triumph by fulfilling a promise to go bungee jumping, was more cryptic when asked whether he had another stunt up his sleeve.
“I have a couple of things in mind,” he said, smiling. “I think you’ll get to know in time, maybe.”

articles.headline: 49ers win in Mexico and Bills stay top - NFL week 11
keyFacts: The San Francisco 49ers defeated the Minnesota Vikings 35-10 in Mexico City, and the Buffalo Bills beat the Miami Dolphins 26-9 to both reach a 9-1 record.
San Francisco will play the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, while Buffalo will face the Kansas City Chiefs on Thursday.
The New York Giants secured a 23-18 home win against the Jacksonville Jaguars to improve to 6-3-1.
body: - Published
The San Francisco 49ers and Buffalo Bills remain the pacesetters in each conference of the NFL after both won again.
The 49ers beat the Minnesota Vikings in the last of a record nine international games this season to take their record to 9-1.
They lead the way in the NFC, with divisional rivals the Chicago Bears and Detroit Lions next best on 8-2.
Buffalo improved to 9-1 for the first time since 1991 and lead the AFC from another pair of divisional rivals, with the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos on 8-2.
The Bills could be joined by the Cincinnati Bengals, who conclude week 11 at the Washington Commanders on Monday.
49ers outsmart Vikings defence
Mexico hosted the first regular-season game to be played outside the US in October 2005, and the NFL returned to the country on Sunday following a four-year absence.

After being redeveloped for the 2026 World Cup, the Azteca Stadium staged its sixth NFL game and the third involving San Francisco, who kicked off this season's international series by beating the Los Angeles Rams in Australia in week one.
Sunday's game pitted the league's best offence against the best defence and was the first international game to be played in the primetime slot.
The Vikings defence had not conceded more than 23 points in a game this season, but the 49ers offence outsmarted them in front of 85,612 fans in Mexico City.
The 49ers scored four touchdowns in the first half - two by George Kittle - before running out 35-10 winners.
Mike Evans returned after missing three games with an Achilles problem to finish with 109 receiving yards and a touchdown.
San Francisco face another test of their Super Bowl credentials on Sunday at home to the defending champions, the 6-4 Seattle Seahawks, who were one of six teams on their bye this week.
Giants secure statement win
The Jacksonville Jaguars entered week 11 with the best regular-season record over the past 12 months - they had lost only twice - and had scored more than 30 points in each of their past four games.
Yet the New York Giants managed to stifle the Jaguars for three quarters and led 20-6 heading into what proved to be a dramatic final quarter.
The Jaguars had to settle for a field goal after a controversial call denied them a touchdown, but they still threatened a fightback as they cut the deficit to five.
The Giants offence did enough to stop the Jags getting one more possession, though, and secure a 23-18 home win.
It was the first time the NFC East leaders have beaten a team with a winning record this season and they are now 6-3-1, while the 7-3 Jags remain in charge of the AFC South.
In his first season as head coach, John Harbaugh could lead the Giants to their first division title since 2011, when 'Big Blue' went on to claim their fourth Super Bowl.
They remain clear of the 5-6 Dallas Cowboys, whose rollercoaster season continued with a 51-30 win over the Tennessee Titans, with Dak Prescott throwing for 325 years and four touchdowns.
Kelce at the double before tough Chiefs run
Although Josh Allen threw for more interceptions than touchdowns (2-1), the Bills were still comfortable, beating the Miami Dolphins 26-9 for their sixth straight victory.
The Bills have a mouth-watering Thanksgiving clash on Thursday (01:20 GMT, Friday) at home to the Kansas City Chiefs, who beat the Arizona Cardinals 34-7.
Travis Kelce had two scores for the Chiefs, claiming multiple touchdowns in the same game for the first time since a play-off win over Buffalo in January 2024.
Emmett Johnson registered a combined 143 yards and a touchdown in the absence of fellow running back Kenneth Walker, who is set to return from a minor groin problem against Buffalo.
That game kicks off a crucial five-game stretch for Kansas City, which continues against the Rams, the Bengals, the Patriots and the 49ers.
The Chiefs are joint top of the AFC West with the Denver Broncos, who kept the pressure on by beating the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24 for a sixth straight win.

Fernando Mendoza, this year's first overall draft pick, threw his first three touchdown passes but then a pick-six which allowed Denver to clinch victory, after Jonah Coleman had run in three scores for the Broncos.
Bears and Lions set up Thanksgiving showdown
The home team won all seven of the early games, and they were favourites heading into all but one of those match-ups.
The only underdogs to emerge victorious were the Philadelphia Eagles (3-7), who beat the Pittsburgh Steelers 19-16 to end a seven-game losing streak.
The Bears and Lions both won to remain joint-top of the NFC North, and they have a Thanksgiving showdown in Detroit on Thursday (18:00 GMT).
The Bears beat the New Orleans Saints 21-13, with Chicago's Jeffery Simmons claiming three sacks, taking his tally to five in three games since his blockbuster trade from Tennessee.
On Thursday he will try to stop this season's rushing leader Jahmyr Gibbs, who rushed for another 98 yards and two touchdowns in Detroit's 31-21 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
The NFL's highest-paid running back has now tied Barry Sanders for the most rushing touchdowns (52) before turning 25 â and Gibbs' birthday is not until March.

articles.headline: Techie turned his too-easy job interview into a trap
keyFacts: Marshall quickly fixed a broken PC during a job interview about twenty years ago by checking common faults.
Marshall suggested to his future manager that setting the power supply to the wrong voltage would make a good test.
Marshall's former manager emailed him years later after a candidate blew a power supply by not checking the voltage.
body: Returning to work after the weekend can feel like voluntarily walking into a trap. To help readers feel a little freer, The Register therefore uses Monday mornings to serve up a new installment of " Who, Me? " It's the column in which we share your stories of mistakes, misjudgments, and occasional misanthropy.
This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Marshall," who told us about a job interview he endured about 20 years ago.
The interview included a practical component he described as "Here's a PC, we've broken a few things in it, get it going."
Marshall quickly spotted some mundane faults, such as a loose PCI card and unplugged internal cables.
He felt the test was too easy. "One of the things I always checked was whether the power supply 110/230 switch was set for the UK," he told The Register .
Getting the PC running earned Marshall a job offer, but he couldn't resist suggesting a tougher test.
"I said to my future manager: 'Would it be a good thing to set the power supply to the wrong voltage as part of the interview test?' He said that wasn't fair."
Marshall stayed in the job for two years. A couple of months after he left, his former manager sent him a short email.
"Ha-ha, very funny."
Marshall asked another former colleague what might have prompted that email.
"It turned out somebody – I don't know if it was an interview candidate – had blown a power supply by not checking the voltage it was set to."
What a coincidence! Or maybe not?
"It wasn't anything to do with me," Marshall insisted. "No idea who it was."

Have you held colleagues to a higher standard than the boss expected? Or left a little trap for them to trip over? In either case, click here to send email to Who, Me? We appreciate the chance to share your stories, and do so with appropriate anonymization so that contributors never step into the jaws of trouble. ®

articles.headline: How to remove Advanced Trackers from cars in GTA 6
keyFacts: Players can remove Advanced Trackers from high-end cars in GTA 6 after progressing past a specific stage in the game.
Destructoid states that players must collect a list of vehicles and a Declassed Mamba GT for a character named Randy.
Destructoid reports that players must then wait 24 hours for Randy to call, after which Pay and Spray outlets can remove the trackers.
body: Advanced trackers are a nuisance in GTA 6 , and they can cause a lot of trouble if you’re not careful. You’ll typically find these on high-end cars in and around Leonida, and dispatching them can be problematic.
However, you do get to remove Advanced Trackers once you have progressed past a specific stage in the game.
How to unlock the ability to remove Advanced Trackers in GTA 6

To commence the process, the first task is to collect vehicles for Randy. Once Randy introduces himself, he will provide you with a list of cars. You have to find and deliver them to Randy to complete the list.

Screenshot by Destructoid Finding 20 cars can be a difficult task, and more so when they’re situated all around Leonida. Thankfully, this guide will make your life simpler . Once you manage to find the first 10, Randy will tell you to steal a Declassed Mamba GT. Unlike other vehicles you have looted until now, the Mamba GT has a specific location.
Make sure you go and check out our sister site, GTA 6 Bible for all your GTA 6 needs.

Once you steal and deliver all cars, you’ll complete the initial set of Randy’s wishlist. You can always repair the car before selling it to Randy for a juicy bonus. This takes place after you complete the Shoot a Promo mission in Chapter 4.

Screenshot by Destructoid Then, wait for 24 hours, and Randy will call you. He will tell you that Pay and Spray outlets can now remove Advanced Trackers. You can confirm this by opening an outlet on the map, and you’ll find the description that they deal in Tracked vehicles.

However, it's below the Bills and the Chiefs, and the 49ers on the other side of the conference divide, where things are really starting to get interesting.

The Denver Broncos (8-2) are also in the mix for top billing in the AFC, after claiming a sixth straight against the Las Vegas Raiders, while the Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) have the opportunity to match that mark with a Monday night victory at the Washington Commanders.

The Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) stumbled at the New York Giants (6-3-1), whose impressive victory strengthened their grip on the NFC East division, which the Dallas Cowboys (5-6) are still in the hunt for after hanging 51 on the Tennessee Titans defense.

The Jaguars' loss was far from fatal, with the Titans, along with the Indianapolis Colts and the Houston Texans all floundering in their division, though the Pittsburgh Steelers' (6-4) shock loss at the Philadelphia Eagles might well have opened the door to the latter in the race for a wildcard berth.

The Texans, who started the season 0-4, now sit 4-6 and - after a meeting with a Baltimore Ravens team in the midst of a six-game losing streak - will likely have the opportunity to match the Steelers' record when the two teams meet in a fortnight, following Pittsburgh's tricky assignment against the Broncos where they'll try to avoid dropping three in a row.

Meanwhile, back in the NFC, the greatest intrigue lies in the NFC North and the four-way battle unfolding for the division, with the Detroit Lions (8-2), Chicago Bears (8-2), Vikings (7-3) - even with their chastening loss to the Niners - and Green Bay Packers (6-4) all currently playoff bound.
Mind you, they all have the looming threat of the wildcard-hunting Los Angeles Rams (6-4) and defending Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks (6-4) from the NFC West.
It makes the Thanksgiving night clash between the Lions and Bears in Detroit - live on Sky Sports NFL from 6pm, Thursday - even more crucial.
See, 'football season (really does) start at Thanksgiving'.
What we learned
The Cowboys' offense is unstoppable!
Quite literally.

Lost in amongst how historically bad their defense is - even the one-win Titans scored on five of their first six possessions, one week on from the 49ers managing to score 46 points and a staggering 584 yards against them - is how impressive their offense is, and needs to be!

The Cowboys are just the fourth team in NFL history to allow at least 20 points in each of their first 11 games and still win at least five of those games. They have allowed 20 points in 18 straight games dating back to Week 12 of last season.

But Dak Prescott threw four touchdown passes and ran in another score as Dallas found the end zone on each of their first six drives in their 51-30 thumping of the Titans to somewhat mask their continued defensive woes.
Fernando Mendoza looks the real deal.

There's still teething issues as the No 1 overall draft picks eases his way into NFL life - most notably the game-sealing pick-six he threw that ensured he starts his career with back-to-back defeats in his first two starts. But there was a lot to like too.
Mendoza and the Raiders hung with the Broncos far longer than many expected, with it being just a one-score game when the rookie QB tossed that costly interception.
Prior to that, he completed 18 of 37 passes for 267 yards and three passing touchdowns - his first in the NFL.
"I felt more comfortable than last week," Mendoza admitted afterwards. "I was able to settle in and able to see the entire field better.
"If you just do your job, your momentum is going to swing your way eventually."
Overreaction or reality?
Are the Steelers in danger of dropping out of the AFC playoff picture?

It certainly looks like they're in trouble. The 19-16 reverse in Philadelphia not only was the Eagles' first win in eight games, it was the Steelers' second straight loss, with Aaron Rodgers, who turns 43 on December 2, looking every bit his age as he limped to 95 passing yards when going 17 of 20 in the first half.

That turned into 227 yards by the end of the game after some garbage-time stat-padding, but it's looking a little rough for the Steelers, who currently occupy the seventh and final playoff berth in the AFC and have a dire run of stellar defenses to come over the next three-week stretch in the Broncos, Texans and Jaguars.

Helping their cause is the fact that the AFC isn't exactly flush with challengers. The New England Patriots (5-5) are currently their closes rivals but they're in the midst of their own crisis with starting quarterback Drake Maye out for the year, then there's the Texans (4-6) and that's pretty much it.
Though Houston's record looks pretty ugly at the minute, they won nine straight from 3-5 to get into the playoffs last year, so are well capable of going on a run.
Their visit to Pittsburgh in two weeks' time could prove pivotal.
Winners and losers
Winners:

David Bailey: The New York Jets rookie edge rusher had two sacks in their win at the Los Angeles Chargers that broke their five-game losing streak, giving him nine-and-a-half sacks on the season to go with six forced fumbles, including one against the Chargers.

The No 2 overall draft pick generated five pressures, meaning he has now recorded 45 pressures this season, the third-most by a rookie defender through Week 11 since 2018, trailing only Jared Verse (50 in 2024) and Nick Bosa (49 in 2019).

Travis Kelce: The veteran Chiefs tight end had 74 receiving yards to go with two receiving touchdowns in their win over the Arizona Cardinals, his first game with multiple receiving touchdowns since Week 11 of the 2022 season against the Chargers.

The 37-year-old's eight-yard score on Kansas City's opening possession also saw him pass Rob Gronkowski into third place for the most total touchdowns (including playoffs) by a tight end in NFL history with 109.
Only Pro Football Hall of Famers Antonio Gates (118) and Tony Gonzalez (115) have scored more.
Losers:

DK Metcalf: The Steelers receiver was ejected from their game in Philadelphia after committing two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties 10 offensive plays apart, with the second of those appearing to see him reach into Cooper DeJean's facemask and poke the defensive back near the eye, sparking a melee between the two teams.
The ejection is Metcalf's third for his career since his debut in 2019. That's tied with 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw for the most in the NFL during that span.

"It's emotional on a number of fronts," Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said afterwards. "We lost a game, a tough game. You take all that in, and everything will be addressed. We can't have players getting ejected from games."
Tennessee Titans: "All gas, no brake" is Tennessee head coach Robert Saleh's much-quoted mantra.
Well, the Titans took that sentiment a touch too literally on Sunday with someone seemingly cutting the breaks as they went careering off a cliff against the Cowboys.
And the coach, renowned for his defensive acumen, was NOT happy about the performance as his defense let up 51 points.
"It was disgusting, embarrassing football," Saleh said afterwards. "That starts with me. I got to figure it out.
"We have no choice but to get better. It can't get any worse."
Player of the Weekend - Jeffery Simmons, DT, Chicago Bears

Jeffery Simmons has been everything the Bears could've hoped for following their blockbuster mid-season trade for the former Titans defensive tackle which saw Chicago cough up two first-round draft picks.

He was the standout from Dennis Allen's unrelenting defense in their victory over the New Orleans Saints in which Chicago racked up a season-high 23 quarterback pressures and six sacks - Simmons recording three of those, tying his career high in a single game.
In doing so, he also became the first Bears defensive tackled to have three sacks in a game since 2014, taking his tally to five in three games since arriving in Chicago.
